Virender Singh, Judge

The appellants have filed the present appeal, under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (hereinafter referred to as 'the M.V. Act'), against the award dated 14.5.2013,
passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-IV, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in Claim Petition No. 29-S/2 of 2011, titled as, 'Smt. .
Kamlesh & others versus Vidya & anr.'.
2.

sentences.text:
Vide award dated 14.5.2013, the learned Tribunal has allowed the petition, filed by the petitioners, under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, and awarded a sum of Rs.4,52,000/- alongwith interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of filing of the petition, till realization of the whole amount,
from the appellants.
However, the ultimate liability to pay the amount, has been fastened upon the Insurance Company.

3. Parties to the lis, hereinafter, are, referred to, in the same manner, in which, they were referred to,
by the learned Tribunal.

4. Brief facts, leading to filing of the present case, may be summed up as under:
Petitioners have filed the petition, under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation, on account of death of Shri Jagdish Verma, husband of petitioner No.
1, father of petitioners No. 2 and 3 and son of petitioner No. 4.

They have sought compensation on the ground that Jagdish Verma was .
travelling in vehicle No. HP-09A-1827 (hereinafter referred to as 'the vehicle in question').

The said vehicle was owned and driven by Sandeep Sagar, who had also Kamlesh & Others vs Vidya & Another on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195557873/
1 expired in the said accident.
As such, respondent No. 1 has been impleaded as his legal heir.

4.1 Elaborating their stand, it is the case of the petitioners that the accident in question had taken place at Taras Dhank, District Kinnaur, on 23.6.2010, whereas,
dead body was found on 25.6.2010 at about 8:30 a.m.
The matter was reported to the Police of Police Station, Pooh, where the FIR was registered.

The age of Jagdish Verma has been pleaded as 33 years, and at the time of death, he was said to be earning Rs.
25,000/- per month.
It is the further case of the petitioners that deceased Jagdish Verma was employed with Bhupender Sharma, S/o Shri Keshav Ram Sharma, Vegetable and Fruit Commission Agent, Sabzi Mandi, Theog.
The accident in question has been pleaded to have taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver.

5. On the basis of above facts, petitioners have .
pleaded their bright past and bleak future.
6. When put to notice, the claim petition has been contested/resisted by the respondents.
7. Respondent No. 1 has filed reply by admitting the factum of accident.
However, income of Jagdish Verma, during his life time, to be Rs. 25,000/- has been denied.
Other contents of the petition have been denied.

8. Insurance Company has also filed its separate reply, by taking preliminary objections that the petition is not maintainable; petition is vague; the vehicle in question was being permitted to ply in violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance policy; and the driver of the vehicle was not having valid and effect driving license, at the time of accident.

9. On the basis of above facts, the learned Tribunal has framed the following issues, vide order dated 25.5.2012:
1.

Whether Sh. Jagdish predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners died on account of rash and negligent driving on part of Sandeep Nagar, the driver of vehicle No.
HP-09A-1827, as alleged?

OPP . 
2. If issue No. 1 is proved in affirmative, whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount?
OPP 3.
Whether the present petition is not maintainable?
OPR 4.
Whether Sandeep Sagar was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident?

OPR2 Kamlesh & Others vs Vidya & Another on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195557873/
2
5. Whether the petition has been filed by the petitioners in collusion with respondent No. 1?
OPR 6.
Whether vehicle No. HP-09A-1827 was being plied by Sandeep Sagar in violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance policy?
OPR2 7. Relief.
10. Thereafter, parties were directed to adduce evidence.

After closure of evidence, upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, the learned Tribunal has passed the award, as referred to above,
which is impugned herein, mainly on the ground of inadequacy of amount of compensation.

Enhancement of award has been sought on the ground that the learned Tribunal has wrongly taken the income of deceased as Rs. 3000/- per month, and the evidence, which has been produced before the learned Tribunal, has not .
been properly considered.
Statement of PW-4, in this regard, is stated to have wrongly been discarded.

11. Similarly, according to the petitioner, the statement of PW-5 and the document proved by him,
as Ext. PW5/A, has also not been considered by the learned Tribunal, in a proper manner.
The learned Tribunal has not given the amount of future prospects, had the deceased been alive.
The amount of compensation on the conventional heads is also stated to be on the lower side.
12. On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the petition, by enhancing the amount of compensation.

13. Per contra, Mr. Deepak Bhasin, Senior Advocate, appearing for respondent No. 2 has supported the award in question on the ground that the learned Tribunal has rightly considered all the aspects of the case, as such, the amount of compensation, does not require any interference, by this Court.

14. Since, in this case, the award passed by the .
learned Tribunal has not been assailed by the Insurance Company, upon whom the liability, has been fastened
, as such, this Court shall confine to the discussions with regard to the fact whether just compensation has been awarded by the learned Tribunal or not.

15. In order to award the just compensation, it would be appropriate for this Court, to discuss the following evidence, adduced by the petitioners, to seek compensation, on account of death of Shri Jagdish Verma.
In the petition, the age of Jagdish Verma has been mentioned, as 33 years.

16. Petitioner No. 1, when appeared in the witness box, as PW-6, has given the age of her husband,
at the time of his death, as 32 years.

However, keeping in view the age, as mentioned in the petition,
Kamlesh & Others vs Vidya & Another on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195557873/
3 as well as, in the post mortem report, the age of deceased Jagdish Verma, is proved to be 33-34 years, at the time of his death.

sentences.text:
17. So far as the income of Shri Jagdish Verma, .
during his life time is concerned, the petitioners have pleaded his income as Rs. 25,000/- per month.

They have bifurcated his salary as Rs. 15,000/- p.m.+ incentive of about 10,000/- per month, as such, they have claimed the income of deceased Jagdish Verma, during his life time, as Rs. 25,000/- per month.
18. To prove his income, they have examined PW-4 Bhupender Sharma.

According to this witness,
Jagdish Verma was working with him.
This witness is dealing in the trade of selling and purchasing fruits, as commission agent.
According to this witness, he used to pay Rs. 15,000/- per month to Jagdish Verma.
Apart from the salary, this witness used to give him incentive.

The salary used to be paid in cash,
whereas, incentive used to be paid through cheque.
He proved his statements of account as Mark-A to mark-D.

In the income tax return, this witness has mentioned the salary of Jagdish Verma as Rs.
15,000/-.
In this regard, he has placed on record the documentary proof as Mark-F to Mark-K.
Jagdish Verma was working with this witness from the year 2005.

In his further .
cross-examination, he has deposed that he is not having any proof, with regard to payment of incentive, but, again reiterated that reference, in this regard, has been made in Mark-A to Mark-D.
Although, the record pertaining to his salary was summoned, but, according to him, the said record has now lost.

19. PW-5 Mast Ram proved the document Ext.
PW5/A.
The said record is of SBI, Theog.
The record was not prepared by him.
20. PW-6 is petitioner No. 1.
She has deposed that her husband used to pay Rs. 15,000/- to her.
Except the income of her husband, the petitioners are having no other source of income.
She is not having any documentary proof, with regard to income of her deceased husband.
21. Learned Tribunal has taken the income of Jagdish Verma, during his life time, as Rs. 3000/- per month.

Although, PW-4 could not produce the documents, which have been marked as Mark-A to mark-D, but, his statement on oath, cannot be brushed aside, merely on the ground that no .
document has been produced by him.
A person, when deposes on oath, his statement carries presumption of truth in it, until or unless, the contrary has been proved, in the cross-examination.

22. Considering the statement of PW-6, that her husband used to pay a sum of Rs. 15000/- to her,
and the statement of PW-4 on oath, this Court is of the view that income of deceased Jagdish Verma,
during his lifetime, could be Rs. 10,000/-per month.

4 23.

sentences.text: Keeping in view the above position, as well as, the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court, in National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, age of deceased Jagdish Verma, at the time of his death, and considering the fact that he was working in Private Sector, 40%, increase is to be given on account of his future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, his monthly income comes to Rs. 10,000+ Rs. 4,000= Rs. 14,000/- per month.
24. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma & Others versus Transport Corporation and Others (2009) 6 .

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Others versus Transport Corporation and Others (2009) 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Supreme

Court Cases, 121, 1/3rd amount is liable to be deducted, on account of personal expenses,
had he been alive.
Thus, his contribution towards his family comes to Rs. 14000- Rs. 4667/- (1/3 rd of 14000/-) = Rs. 9333/- per month.

25. So far as the multiplier is concerned, the multiplier of 16 would be just and proper, in this case,
which has rightly been applied by the learned Tribunal.
26.

In view of the discussion made above, the award passed by the learned Tribunal is liable to be modified and the same is modified accordingly and the compensation, for which the petitioners are held entitled, is assessed as under:

1. Loss of contribution: Rs. 9333x12x16= Rs. 17,91,936/-.
2. Loss of estate :Rs. 15,000/-
3. Funeral expenses : Rs. 15,000/-
4. Loss of consortium : Rs.40,000x 4 = Rs. 1,60,000/-
Total: Rs.17,91,936+15000+15000+1,60,000/= Rs.
19,81,936/-.
27.

Consequently, the petitioners are held entitled .
for the amount of Rs. 19,81,936/-. alongwith interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of filing of petition, till realization of amount.
The aforesaid amount be apportioned amongst the petitioners, as ordered by the learned Tribunal.
28. The appeal is, thus, allowed in the aforesaid terms.
Pending application(s), if any, are also disposed of accordingly.
Memo of costs be prepared.
29. Record be sent down.
(Virender Singh) Judge January 12, 2023 Kalpana Kamlesh & Others vs Vidya & Another on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195557873/
